subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.iv@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Hi Sasha / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Below is a brief recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update the plan.

Summary of your pain / goals
- Current pain: production latency spikes and unpredictable per-request cost when you batch user requests across multiple tenants.
- Security/isolation: regulatory requirement to isolate sensitive models/traffic for a subset of customers (PCI/financial PII).
- Predictability: you need predictable TPS and guaranteed capacity for peak batch processing windows (end of day risk-scoring jobs).
- Success criteria: 100ms median token latency for API calls under SLA, predictable throughput of ~12 TPS sustained for inference pipelines, per-tenant isolation, and cost within 20% of current baseline after optimizations.

Current stack (as described)
- Frontend: internal microservices calling an API gateway; requests fan out to an ML inference layer.
- Inference today: mixed self-hosted GPUs + cloud inference instances (custom orchestration). Models are a mix of open sizes (base and fine-tuned) and a proprietary ranking model.
- Monitoring: internal Prometheus + Grafana; limited visibility into per-token cost and KV-cache hit rates.

Dedicated fit / recommended config we discussed
- Reserved GPU pools: single-tenant Dedicated cluster with reserved capacity for Aurora workloads to provide workload isolation and predictable throughput.
- Throughput sizing: initial footprint recommendation = 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (we estimate this gives ~12 sustained TPS for your 2k-context ranking pipeline with our runtime optimizations).
- Autoscaling & burst: recommended baseline pool + burst capacity policy (allow up to 2x capacity for short windows) to handle batch windows. Autoscaling triggers based on queue latency and token backlog.
- Isolation: network-level VPC peering + dedicated tenancy; data plane separation and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Cost levers: quantization recommendations for ranking models, prefix/KV caching, and batching to reduce per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs.

Risks / unknowns we called out
- Model memory footprint and exact throughput depend on final quantization and kernel selection — we’ll confirm during the technical deep dive.
- Peak patterns: we need historical 30/90-day traffic to finalize autoscale thresholds.

Success metrics (to validate during pilot)
- Median token latency <= 100ms for 95% of requests
- Sustained 12 TPS for the ranked inference pipeline without SLA violations
- Demonstrated per-tenant isolation and audit logs for sample requests
- Cost reduction target: <= 20% delta vs current infra after batching/quantization improvements

Next steps / action items
1) Technical deep-dive: propose Mon/Thu next week — 60m with your infra/ML engineering team to review model sizes, traffic patterns, and confirm sizing. (Marissa to propose times).
2) You to share: historical traffic (30/90 day), representative model artifacts (weights + config), and current SLOs.
3) Redwood to send: preliminary Mutual Action Plan and a Dedicated capacity one-pager (attached).
4) Procurement: we can provide a draft commercial term preview ahead of the technical deep-dive if helpful.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf (summary + sizing guide), mutual-action-plan-aurora.xlsx (preliminary tasks & timeline).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through this recap.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference (hosted, dedicated, private).

From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.iv@aurorafin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@aurorafin.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Thanks Marissa — good write-up and aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 12 TPS target looks right for peak scoring windows; during daily batches we can burst higher but only for short windows (10-15 minutes).
- On isolation: we need audit logs retained for 1 year and proof of encryption-at-rest using a customer-managed key. Confirm that fits the Dedicated offering.
- Procurement question: what is the minimum contract term for Dedicated reserved pools? Also can you share an example support SLA for enterprise (response / priority)?

Priya (copied) will own gathering traffic samples and model artifacts — she’ll follow up with the 30/90-day metrics.

One more ask: do you have a simple TCO estimate for the 4x A100 configuration vs our current mixed cloud fleet? A ballpark would help with our procurement scoping.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of ML Platforms | Aurora Finance
Sasha.Iv@aurorafin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.iv@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Thanks Sasha — all great questions. Quick answers inline: 

- Burst windows: yes, we can support 10-15 minute bursts up to 2x capacity; we’ll capture the specific autoscale policy in the MAP.
- Audit logs & KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and we can retain audit logs for 12 months; we’ll include the retention configuration in the deployment spec.
- Minimum term: our standard Dedicated reserved pools are 12 months minimum; we can discuss pilot shorter-term options (90d pilot + commit) if procurement needs flexibility.
- Support SLA: I’ll attach the enterprise SLA excerpt and include typical response times (P1/P2).
- TCO: Rafael will prepare a ballpark TCO for 4x A100 vs your current fleet — Rafael, can you take the lead and include assumptions (utilization, reserved vs on-demand pricing)?

Next steps: I’ll send a calendar invite for a technical deep-dive Tuesday 6/16 11:00am PT (please confirm) and follow up with the MAP + SLA excerpt.

Thanks!
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
